guide.title: Bites, Stings & Envenomation
guide.lead: Most bites and stings need wound care and calm. The killers are anaphylaxis, which needs IM epinephrine immediately, and venomous snakes, which need immobilisation, rapid transport and antivenom – not cutting, sucking, ice or tourniquets.

sections.title: Anaphylaxis?
sections.question: After a sting or bite: breathing difficulty, throat or tongue swelling, low blood pressure, or collapse – with or without hives?
sections.yes: Epinephrine IM into the outer thigh now (0.01 mg/kg, maximum 0.5 mg; auto-injector 0.3 mg, or 0.15 mg for small children). Repeat after 5 minutes if no better. Lie flat (or sit up if breathless), oxygen, IV fluids.
sections.no: Local reaction: remove the sting, wash, cold pack, antihistamine for itch; watch for spread.

steps.title: Away from the snake
steps.text: Don't try to catch or kill it; a photo from a distance helps.

steps.title: Calm and still
steps.text: Remove rings and watches; splint the limb at about heart level; carry, don't walk.

steps.title: Mark it
steps.text: Outline the edge of swelling with the time every 15 minutes.

steps.title: Neurotoxic snakes (elapids: coral snakes, cobras, kraits, Australian snakes)
steps.text: A firm pressure-immobilisation bandage over the whole limb where local guidelines advise. Not for North American pit vipers.

steps.title: Go
steps.text: Rapid transport to a hospital with antivenom; watch airway (paralysis), bleeding and blood pressure.

sections.title: Never
items: Tourniquet or tight band (except pressure-immobilisation where indicated)

sections.title: Other bites and stings
rows: Remove a bee sting fast by any method – speed matters more than scraping
Severe cramps, rigid abdomen without peritonitis, sweating
Pain relief, benzodiazepines for spasm per protocol, hospital
Painless bite, later red-white-blue lesion, necrosis
Vinegar for box jellyfish and many tropical species; then hot water (about 45 °C) for pain
Hot water as hot as tolerated (about 45 °C) for 30–90 minutes; wound care, X-ray for spine fragments
Irrigate well; cat and human bites infect easily; rabies and tetanus per local guidance

quiz.q: Snakebite to the hand: two punctures, mild pain, little swelling, normal vital signs. Best care?
options: Remove rings, splint at about heart level, mark the swelling, transport
quiz.explanation: Calm, still, transport for possible antivenom.

quiz.q: Bee sting: hives, lip and tongue swelling, wheeze, BP 80/50. Priority?
options: Epinephrine IM into the outer thigh
quiz.explanation: Epinephrine first; the others are add-ons.

quiz.q: Surfer steps on something in shallow sea water: a foot puncture with pain out of proportion. Most likely, and care?
options: Stingray: hot water as hot as tolerated (about 45 °C) for 30–90 minutes, irrigate, X-ray

quiz.q: A child bitten by an unidentified snake: no pain or swelling, then drooping eyelids and slurred speech 2 hours later. Most likely?
options: Neurotoxic (elapid, e.g. coral snake) envenomation: airway watch, antivenom
quiz.explanation: Minimal local signs don't exclude neurotoxic venom.
Repeat after 5 minutes if no improvement.

options: Neurotoxic snakes such as Australian elapids, per local guidance
quiz.explanation: It slows lymphatic spread of neurotoxic venom.

options: As fast as possible by any method

quiz.q: Severe abdominal cramps and rigidity without tenderness after a spider bite. Suspect:
quiz.explanation: Pain relief and benzodiazepines for spasm.

flashcards.question: Venomous snake types
flashcards.answer: Vipers (rattlesnakes, adders, Russell's viper): local swelling, bleeding, low BP. Elapids (cobras, kraits, coral snakes, most Australian snakes): neurotoxic paralysis, often little local reaction.

flashcards.question: Snakebite DON'Ts
flashcards.answer: No cutting, sucking, tourniquets (except pressure-immobilisation where advised), ice, electric shock or alcohol. Don't chase the snake.

flashcards.question: Black widow
flashcards.answer: Severe cramps, rigid abdomen without peritonitis, sweating, high BP. Pain relief, benzodiazepines, hospital.

flashcards.question: Brown recluse
flashcards.answer: Painless bite that becomes a red, white and blue lesion and may necrose. Wound care and follow-up.

flashcards.question: Anaphylaxis treatment
flashcards.answer: Epinephrine IM into the outer thigh: 0.01 mg/kg, maximum 0.5 mg (auto-injector 0.3 mg; 0.15 mg for small children). Repeat after 5 minutes. Oxygen, fluids.

flashcards.question: Bee stings
flashcards.answer: Remove fast by any method. Watch for anaphylaxis.

flashcards.question: Jellyfish vs stingray
flashcards.answer: Jellyfish: vinegar (box jellyfish and many tropical species), then hot water. Stingray and venomous fish: hot water about 45 °C for 30–90 minutes.

flashcards.question: Viper vs coral snake bite
flashcards.answer: Viper: immediate pain, swelling, bruising, bleeding. Coral snake: little local reaction; neurotoxic signs (ptosis, slurred speech, weakness) may be delayed for hours.

critical.scenario: Hiker bitten on the lower leg by a rattlesnake 20 minutes ago: swelling spreading up the shin, tingling lips, metallic taste.
critical.question: Complete prehospital care?

options.t: Remove jewellery, splint at about heart level, mark the swelling edge and time, carry him, IV access, monitor, rapid transport to an antivenom hospital; no cut, suck, tourniquet or ice

critical.explanation: Tingling lips and metallic taste mean systemic envenomation.

critical.scenario: 7-year-old (22 kg) stung by a bee 15 minutes ago: widespread hives, hoarse voice, wheeze, lips swelling.
critical.question: Assessment and treatment?

options.t: Anaphylaxis: epinephrine IM 0.01 mg/kg into the outer thigh (or the 0.15 mg auto-injector), oxygen, position of comfort, repeat after 5 minutes if needed, transport

options.f: Doesn't treat the swelling or shock.

options.t: Wait to see if it settles

critical.explanation: Observe in hospital; reactions can return.
critical.kpi: Recognizes pediatric anaphylaxis and gives IM epinephrine

critical.scenario: Traveller in northern Australia bitten on the ankle by a brown snake while walking; little pain, no swelling.
critical.question: First aid?

options.t: Pressure-immobilisation bandage over the whole limb and a splint, keep still, call for transport to an antivenom hospital
Nothing: no swelling means no venom
options.f: Australian elapids cause little local reaction.
Don't wash: hospitals may test venom from the site.

critical.kpi: Applies pressure-immobilisation for an elapid bite
